title: It's Groundhog Day, and the real groundhogs are asleep
body: Every groundhog {place} is curled up underground right now, hearts beating just a few times a minute. They won't come out to check for shadows until the ground warms up in March. Let them sleep.

kicker: Big moment · First sign of spring
title: The red-wings are back
body: It's still cold, but the first red-winged blackbirds are already shouting conk-la-ree from last year's cattails near {water}. To a lot of birders, that sound is the real first day of spring.

title: Spring migration is peaking
body: Right now, millions of birds are flying north through the night, and many stop in city parks to rest and eat. On some mornings the trees near {green} are suddenly full of birds who weren't there yesterday.

title: The dawn chorus is at its loudest
body: This is the best few weeks of the year for birdsong. Before sunrise, robins start, then cardinals, song sparrows and catbirds join in until the whole block is singing. Open a window early one morning.

title: Baby season on the water
body: Goslings, ducklings and fuzzy gray cygnets are out on the water near {water}, following their parents in wobbly lines. The parents are protective right now, so give the families plenty of room.

title: The babies are out of the nest
body: Spotty young robins, fluffy sparrows and loud young crows are hopping around {place}, not quite flying yet. Their parents are close by and still feeding them. If you see one on the ground, they're almost always fine.

title: The fireflies are here
body: On warm nights right now, slow yellow flashes rise from the grass near {green} just after sunset. It only lasts a few weeks. Turn off the porch light and give them the dark.

title: The chimney swifts are gathering
body: Before they leave for the Amazon, chimney swifts gather at dusk by the hundreds and swirl into one big chimney together, like smoke pouring backward. Watch the sky above {street} at sunset.

title: The monarchs are passing through
body: Monarchs are drifting south past the city right now, stopping on goldenrod and asters near {green}, on their way to mountains in Mexico they've never seen.

title: The hawks are on the move
body: Hawks and falcons are streaming south along the coast right now, riding the wind. Look up on a clear day with a northwest breeze: kestrels, Cooper's hawks and peregrines are passing right over {place}.

kicker: Big moment · A big migration night
title: Tonight is a big migration night
body: A north wind is blowing, and that's what migrating birds wait for. Tonight, birds will pour south over the city in the dark, high above the streetlights. Tomorrow morning, the hedges near {green} may be full of new faces.

kicker: Big moment · Back from the Arctic
title: The brant are back in the harbor
body: Rafts of little sea geese are arriving on {water} from the Arctic tundra, murmuring as they bob. The buffleheads are close behind. Winter on the water is starting.

title: The first frost is here
body: The grass is crunchy and white this morning. The last crickets have gone quiet, the sparrows are fluffed into round little balls, and the squirrels are digging up acorns they buried last month.

title: The longest night of the year
body: Tonight is the winter solstice. The crows head to their big roost early, the day birds sleep for fifteen hours, and the raccoons and opossums get their longest night out. From tomorrow, the days start growing again.

title: It's a snow day
body: Everything {place} is hushed and white. The juncos are hopping in it, the cardinals are glowing red against it, and the squirrels are digging through it for acorns. Look for tracks: tiny hops, little hands, birds' feet.

title: It's a heat wave
body: Everyone is slowing down. Squirrels are splooting belly-flat on shady branches, pigeons are lined up on the shady side of every building, and the bees are visiting flowers early before the heat. A shallow dish of water helps a lot today.
